summary: The first C-only output at step 54 is the result of a polymorphed hero succubus landing an AD_SEDU attack on the adjacent orc-captain. uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_sedu calls steal_it() in its hero-attacker arm; the JavaScript arm still records note_unported('uhitm.c steal_it') and sets damage to zero, so it omits the C inventory transfer and “You steal:” prompt. The complete bounded source task is uhitm.c:theft_petrifies, steal_it, and mhitm_ad_sedu, with the existing damageum -> mhitm_adtyping caller retained.

source.branch: When a polymorphed hero lands an AD_SEDU item-theft attack against a monster, mhitm_ad_sedu delegates to steal_it. steal_it selects one item unless the target is seducible and wearing body armor, temporarily keeps monster gold out of the selection, transfers stolen items through hold_another_object, handles petrifying corpses and worn gear, and restores gold in source order.
callers: uhitm.c:damageum() (4835-4883) calls mhitm_adtyping(); its AD_SITM and AD_SEDU cases (4782-4832) call mhitm_ad_sedu(). JavaScript follows uhitm.js:damageum -> mhitm_adtyping -> mhitm_ad_sedu; this is the selected hero-polymorph entry path.
uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_ssex() (4751-4779) delegates to mhitm_ad_sedu() for its hero-attacker path and its non-specialized monster paths. The existing JavaScript mhitm_ad_ssex() has the corresponding calls.
mhitu.c:mattacku() calls uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() for monster-versus-hero attacks; JavaScript mhitu.js dispatches through uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping().
mhitm.c:mdamagem() calls uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() for monster-versus-monster attacks; JavaScript mhitm.js:mdamagem() dispatches through uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping().
dependencies: steal_it() consumes theft_petrifies() as a boolean; both are in this uhitm.c task.

theft_petrifies() consumes mondata.c:touch_petrifies() (pure and already ported in js/mondata.js) and calls trap.c:instapetrify() with a discarded void result (the existing js/trap.js implementation handles the hero death path).
steal_it() consumes mhitu.c:could_seduce(), steal.c:findgold(), and invent.c:hold_another_object(); the corresponding existing JS functions are in mhitu.js, steal.js, and invent.js.

steal_it() calls steal.c:mpickobj(), worn.c:extract_from_minvent(), weapon.c:possibly_unwield(), and trap.c:mselftouch() with discarded results; mpickobj, extract_from_minvent, and possibly_unwield have existing JavaScript implementations. trap.c:mselftouch is only partially implemented in trap_effects.js because its minstapetrify path is unported; preserve that void gap as note_unported('trap.c mselftouch') without using a result.
